value.problem_keywords: review-bot tickets clone divergence deploy convergence rsync git ancestry
value.propositions: The AWS review-bot's persistent tickets clone on an EBS volume is not refreshed by redeploy because it is cloned behind a conditional guard and lives outside the Dockerfile layer lifecycle. Scripts like reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh are not deployed when only they change because autodeploy.sh's rsync gate (BOT_PATHS) does not include infra/scripts/ paths, creating a chicken-and-egg problem. The tickets clone can diverge from origin/tickets (no shared tip) and the current ensure script does not detect or repair divergence. The review-bot writes code_review tickets and pushes on every Gerrit vote with REBAR_SYNC_PUSH set to always, independent of AWS schedule pausing. Vote safety must be preserved: votes are recorded before artifact emission, and store failures are caught and logged without failing the review gate.

value.propositions: Changes landing on main do not auto-reflect in the running Gerrit environment without manual deploy and restart, causing drift between main and deployed state. A systemd timer-triggered idempotent deploy script (with flock guards and change detection per component) must fetch origin/main and apply only changed components (review-bot, replication.config, g2p config) within ~5 min. Auto-deploy must never touch the gerrit container, refs/meta/config, or trigger a Gerrit restart; health checks and rollback (to prior image) must self-heal broken deploys without freezing the gate. Consecutive deploy failures (≥2) of the same SHA must disable auto-deploy via stop-file and page; malformed config must be rejected pre-apply with prior config retained. In-flight reviews dropped by bot restart are recovered by reconciler backfill; post-deploy canary confirms end-to-end gate health before deployed-sha is advanced.

value.propositions: bridge_fsck reads prev_snapshot.json as an offline Jira oracle and depends on field values for drift classification. value.problem_keywords: many-to-many tracker projects bridge multi-project codebase repos ticket store project scope cross-project
value.propositions: Bridge is hard-wired to exactly one tracker project at three points: JiraConfig.project scalar, fetcher JQL pair, and applier CrossProjectTargetError guard, preventing teams from syncing multiple projects against one shared store. Model many-to-many as one shared ticket store with N repos and N tracker projects; each ticket records its project and repos; the store owns the canonical project set in .bridge_state/projects.json to prevent per-repo disagreement on remote state. Ticket project field is tri-state (absent=legacy, explicit-empty=never sync, explicit key=sync there); migration uses an ensure unit with zero events to resolve absent projects against recorded legacy default. Outbound dispatch must respect per-ticket explicit project or repo default, and guard must accept any project in the configured set, not just one. A store with multiple projects must carry multi-project-bridge capability stamp in .store-compat.json and reject writes from binaries lacking it; single-project stores remain compatible with older binaries.

value.key_entities: rebar.attach_commits src/rebar/_lib_writes.py:697 src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py src/rebar/_cli/__init__.py src/rebar/_commands/attach_commits.py src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py src/rebar/_mcp_writes.py src/rebar/_mcp_models.py COMMITS event rebar-ticket: trailer file_impact git rev-parse git show --name-only
value.problem_keywords: attach_commits repair verb commit linking file_impact validation close gate check deterministic
value.propositions: A new CLI verb `rebar attach-commits <ticket> <sha>...` exposes retroactive commit linking across three surfaces (CLI, library, MCP) with all-or-nothing validation of SHAs before recording any COMMITS event. Invalid SHAs are rejected by calling `git rev-parse --verify <sha>^{commit}` in a shared DET module `commit_impact.py` that imports no `rebar.llm` dependencies. A deterministic close-gate check in `close_precheck.py` blocks close if any discovered commit's changed paths are not covered by the ticket or its transitive descendants' `file_impact` declarations, with specified exemptions (`tests/**`, `docs/**`, `**/*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`). Path matching uses centralized `**/`-aware glob semantics via a single implementation in `commit_impact.glob_match` that both existing copies (`prompts._glob_match`, `registry._glob_match`) delegate to. Commit discovery unions both attached COMMITS events and local commits carrying `rebar-ticket:` trailers or matching subject prefixes; scope symmetry compares against the union of `file_impact` over the same id set. Unresolvable source-(ii) commits fail closed (block), while unreadable source-(i) SHAs (potentially from other clones) are skipped to prevent false positives on the repair surface.

value.propositions: The tickets branch is 1.04 GiB; 92% is reconciler .bridge_state cache due to scattered edits across 18 MB bindings.json defeating git delta compression, with marginal cost of 12.79 KB per version today. Bookkeeping fields baseline_advanced_at (1144 entries changed per pass, never read) and last_get_pass (20 entries, rotation only) accumulate mutations unrelated to actual ticket data, causing unnecessary churn. Deleting the timestamp baseline_advanced_at and moving last_get_pass to a sidecar file reduces marginal packed cost to 1.74 KB and 12.8x total reduction respectively. The .bridge_state cache must remain committed on-branch because the reconciler runs on ephemeral GitHub runners; durable state lives in git, and re-homing off-branch was evaluated and rejected. History reclaim uses a stock git fast-export/filter/fast-import pipeline to reduce real branch from 1.17 GB to 98.8 MB (8.4%) while preserving all commits, merges, and making HEAD tree byte-identical to pre-rewrite.

Retryable gap_reasons (review-error, llm-unavailable, scanner, gate-disabled) should defer voting and remain vote-less so the backfill reconciler can automatically re-drive within RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS. The review_attempts ledger (keyed by change_id, revision) must be shaped to support bb9b's contributor re-trigger reset mechanism and must be separate from the existing voted table. The reviewbot-ensure-tickets.sh script lacks divergence detection and reset logic; it only sets git config and runs ensures. Vote casting must not regress; store emission failures are already wrapped in exception handlers that preserve the cast vote.

value.problem_keywords: importerror lazy import editable install release directory race condition file_impact close precheck
value.propositions: rebar transition <id> in_progress closed fails with ImportError: cannot import name 'commit_impact' from 'rebar._engine_support' when the release directory is deleted mid-process by an updater or garbage-collector while a close command is running. The published runtime uses an editable install (site-packages contains only .pth pointing to <release>/src), so deletion of the release directory breaks lazy imports that occur after the import root vanishes. commit_impact is imported lazily inside _check_file_impact_vs_diff, which runs late in a close after the completion-verifier gate (minutes-long window), creating a race window where prune_releases() or uv tool install --force can delete the backing directory. The root cause is not a packaging defect; the file is present in the source tree, included in wheels, and not gitignored. The defect is a race between release-lifetime management and lazy import timing in editable installs.

value.propositions: Operator-attested evidence currently lacks provenance context (environment, principal, privilege posture, instrument), allowing escapes where attestations are satisfied but measurements came from wrong environments or under broader privilege than production. Two real escapes in run 061c-ecd1-8967-4a76 exploited this gap: measurements from account 579718921998/us-east-2 attested for work targeting 896586841071/us-east-1, and live calls under bedrock:* privilege offered as validation of scoped bedrock:InvokeModel grant. Proposed solution forces measurement provenance (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) into the attestation record as a required continuation line under [operator-attested] checkboxes, in canonical single-line form with non-placeholder values. A deterministic check (det_measurement_provenance.py) validates presence and shape of provenance fields; an AGENT-tier criterion (project.measurement-provenance) judges the declaration against repo facts (IaC backend names, authorization scopes, instrument appropriateness for authorization claims). The instrument field is load-bearing: simulation and static-analysis cannot distinguish from live-call, yet they are not interchangeable evidence for authorization claims (escape 2b: simulate-principal-policy gave wrong confident answer that only real call refuted). The new criterion ships advisory to `.rebar/` project overlay only, leaving shipped contract text and cross-client defaults unchanged, with corpus replay per ADR-0054 deciding later promotion to blocking.

value.propositions: Four modules have unconditional module-top `import fcntl` that blocks collection on non-POSIX platforms; `import rebar` transitively fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fcntl'` on Windows sweep tier. The autouse network guard in tests/conftest.py patches socket.socket.connect for all address families, incorrectly rejecting AF_UNIX (local IPC) used by multiprocessing forkserver on py3.14 Linux. The socket guard narrowing must allow AF_UNIX/AF_LOCAL while blocking only AF_INET/AF_INET6 (real network) to permit forkserver IPC without sacrificing network isolation. Four fcntl imports must be guarded with module-top try/except ImportError→None (or equivalent if/platform or function-local) to match established portability-guard invariant in six sibling modules. On POSIX platforms, guarding the four fcntl imports produces zero behavior change; on non-POSIX, fcntl binds to None and subsequent lock calls raise AttributeError (acceptable—Windows locking out of scope).

value.key_entities: _compact_locked _build_authorship_ledger authorship.build_ticket_position_commit_map authorship.build_position_commit_map resolve_event_commit compact_txn.py:72 attest/authorship.py:294 attest/authorship.py:466 compact.py:275 compact.py:386 git log --full-history --diff-filter=A write_lock_is_busy _commit_backfill _sweep_position_map position_commits
value.problem_keywords: store-wide compaction sweep stalls git log full-history walk per ticket write lock contention critical section performance history walk under lock per-event wildcard pathspec fallback
value.propositions: The store-wide compaction sweep performs one `git log --full-history` walk per ticket inside the store write lock, blocking all writers for minutes; deployed reality is worse — per-ticket map misses fall through to per-event wildcard walks with leading pathspecs that defeat pruning. The history walk is read-only and never needed the write lock; hoisting it out and building one prebuilt position-keyed map per sweep (before any lock) removes the entire git-log cost from the critical section. `_commit_backfill` stages with unscoped `git add -A`, allowing a concurrent writer's in-flight event files to be swept into the compaction commit; scoping to folded paths only prevents this. The sweep never re-yields mid-run; `run_sweep` probes `write_lock_is_busy` once before starting, and the per-ticket loop never probes again, so writers arriving after the sweep starts wait for the entire run. The position-keyed `build_position_commit_map` primitive is the correct one-pass replacement; a path-keyed sibling would miss every lookup and silently restore per-event walks with correct output and no error to notice. The new map parameter on `_build_authorship_ledger` must be optional (keyword, default None) because `compact_rebuild.py` and six existing test call sites pass arguments positionally; the rebuild path folds one ticket where per-ticket walk cost is already correct.

value.problem_keywords: loose object ENOENT git write-tree failure authorship fixture detached maintenance concurrent repack missing reachable blob
value.propositions: The real-history authorship fixture's temporary Git repository intermittently loses freshly committed reachable blobs before merge, causing invalid-object and write-tree failures. Git >=2.47 auto-maintenance spawns detached child processes (git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach) that can repack concurrently with fixture writes, causing blob loss. The fixture omits ADR 0051 foreground-maintenance pins (gc.autoDetach=false, maintenance.autoDetach=false), allowing ambient Git maintenance to escape synchronous fixture control. Pinning both foreground-maintenance settings eliminates the race and preserves all reachable committed blobs deterministically. The defect is fixture-local; no production caller behavior depends on detached maintenance in this code path.

The foreign HEAD value is identical across repeated invocations minutes apart, indicating a stuck/foreign read from a shared temp-checkout colliding under concurrent multi-agent load, not a live race against origin/main advancing. The unscoped whole-HEAD currency check reads git rev-parse HEAD of the evaluator's working tree but compares it against a gate-ref sha (verified_at_sha/origin/main at review time), creating an asymmetry that yields spurious stale-head when the working tree is on a diverged branch. The fix resolves the current gate-ref sha locally (resolve_ref) for attested opcerts and compares to the signed verified_at_sha anchor, preserving whole-HEAD invalidation semantics while reading the correct value. Legacy opcerts without verified_at_sha must keep the existing head_sha working-tree read unchanged to maintain backward compatibility.

The epoch value is an ISO-8601 UTC instant string plus random suffix (e.g. '2026-08-14T09-31-07Z-4f2a'), treated as opaque for byte-equality comparison; non-string values are corrupt. Guard placement must not block ff-adopt convergence at sync.py:101-104 (wedging behind clones) or lock acquisition at lock.py:296 (deadlocking rejection), and at push.py the retry loop must return immediately (not break) to surface PUSH_PENDING on mismatch.

value.propositions: Gates cannot audit measurement provenance because evidence is attested post-hoc; plan-review runs before measurement occurs and completion-verifier accepts operator attestation by design. Measurements taken in wrong environment (wrong AWS account/region) or under broader privilege than production generate green signals that cannot have observed the claimed failure. value.propositions: Gates accept operator-attested evidence without enforcing presence of measurement provenance fields (environment, principal, privilege posture), allowing claims whose context contradicts project reality. Evidence generated under broader privilege than production (e.g., wildcard IAM identity vs scoped role) cannot structurally fail and thus carries zero information about production correctness. value.problem_keywords: stale clone epoch guard store incompatibility union merge fail-closed push retry divergent history
value.propositions: Stale clones with byte-identical early commits bypass unrelated-histories logic and reach the diverged path, allowing silent re-union of ~1 GiB stripped history instead of refusing. A guard in sync.py alone is bypassed because push.py:203 and :229 invoke independent git merge and retry without consulting sync.py, exploiting the code-review artifact creation path. An epoch field must be added to .store-compat.json (not a parallel marker) and guards placed inside sync._union_merge and before push.py merges to abort on epoch mismatch while preserving ff-adopt convergence. The guard must distinguish eight state-matrix cases including two distinct absences (record-absent vs epoch-absent) and corrupt-record, aborting only on mismatch or corruption; git show non-zero must distinguish unreadable ref from absent file in log output. Epoch value is an opaque ISO-8601 UTC instant plus random suffix, compared only for byte equality; older binaries must not error when reading unknown epoch field, and remote state is read via git show, not local worktree. At sync._union_merge the guard must return without merging (no-op degradation); at push.py the guard must return from push_tickets_branch (not break) to surface PUSH_PENDING and avoid silent commit loss.

value.problem_keywords: store compatibility format version capability gate fail-closed forward compatibility migration data loss prevention
value.propositions: An old binary can compute incomplete state from unknown events and emit stale data without a committed store-format-version record that fails closed on incompatible capability. A fail-closed capability gate must be inserted at lock.acquire() (the single convergence point for all write-lock holders) to block all mutating operations when an incompatible record is present. An absent compatibility record must be treated as legacy format 0 and pass-through; the ensure unit idempotently writes it on next init/fsck-repair/MCP-boot, and a missed sweep must not block writes. A corrupt or unreadable record must fail closed (not treated as absent) with a diagnostic naming the parse error, whereas incompatible format_version or required_capabilities entries block all mutations except read-only operations. Explicit gates must be added to fsck_recover_cli and reconcile._apply_mutations() for raw-git and outbound-Jira paths respectively, since they do not call lock.acquire().

value.problem_keywords: git fetch timeout unscoped fetch oversized branch transfer snapshot resolution ref materialization common object database bloat
value.propositions: resolve_ref performs an unscoped git fetch origin before ref resolution, causing all remote heads to be fetched and transferred into the code checkout's common object database. Reviewing origin/main against a remote also hosting a much larger tickets branch pulls unrelated tickets history, bloating the shared pack storage to 11+ GiB and causing fetch timeouts after 300s. The clone's refspec +refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/* applies to the unfiltered fetch, updating refs/remotes/origin/tickets and transferring unreachable-from-main objects unnecessarily. A scoped fetch to only the requested ref (e.g., origin/main) completes in <22s and excludes unrelated branches, proving the oversized transfer is avoidable. Snapshot materialization must scope the opening fetch to the specific requested ref and skip the fetch entirely for locally-present full SHAs to preserve freshness while avoiding unrelated head transfers.

value.key_entities: src/rebar/_snapshot/janitor.py:53 DEFAULT_FREE_WATERMARK_BYTES rebar-root-disk-pressure alarm infra/terraform/monitoring_autodeploy.tf:226 REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:113 tempfile.gettempdir() store_root() tickets- entries free_watermark_pct RECLAIM_TARGET_MARGIN_PCT
value.problem_keywords: root disk pressure disk exhaustion snapshot garbage collection reclaim watermark snapshot janitor container writable layer reviewer unhealthy
value.propositions: On a 30-GiB root volume, the janitor's absolute 2-GiB free-space watermark is crossed only at 93.3% used, which exceeds both the 85% CloudWatch alarm floor and the 90% peak actually observed, so reclaim never engages before the alarm fires. Every review materializes a fresh ~620 MiB copy of the ticket tree on a cache key (tickets branch tip) that advances every ~26 seconds with minimal deltas, producing ~0.85 GiB per review and growth rates of 2.5–10 GiB/h, matching the observed 4.4 GiB/h. The snapshot store lives on the container's writable layer (root disk) because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR is unset everywhere, so store_root() defaults to tempfile.gettempdir(), and the review-bot service has no volume mount covering /tmp. The 7-day cold-trim reclaim trigger is dead code on a container with a ~4-hour lifetime (23 recreations in 4 days), so free-space watermark is the only live trigger and its failure leaves no fallback. The byte-total backstop promised by ADR 0005 and the janitor docstring is not implemented in _gc_pass; materialize_tickets bypasses cache.acquire so add_bytes is never called, leaving the dominant store entries unaccounted. Docker builder prune and image prune cannot reclaim a running container's writable layer; the 12.6-GiB reclaim and the identical 48% floor across 23 independent events prove the bytes belong to an ephemeral layer destroyed on container recreation, not variable-residue pruning.

value.propositions: bridge_fsck reads prev_snapshot.json from disk as an offline Jira oracle and passes field values into ObservedJira.PRESENT for drift classification, making it an out-of-band consumer vulnerable to field absence when prev is narrowed to a key-set. value.key_entities: UV_TOOL_DIR rebar.metrics rebar._engine_support rebar._logging plan_review.registry criteria_routing.json sys.executable site-packages/.pth editable install release directory current symlink
value.problem_keywords: concurrent process deletion release lifetime lazy import failure editable install garbage collection race import error file not found process isolation
value.propositions: A running rebar process can fail with ImportError or FileNotFoundError when an external process deletes or force-reinstalls the backing release directory during process execution. Lazy imports of modules like rebar.metrics and rebar._engine_support fail because the editable install's .pth file points to a source directory that no longer exists, even though the module code was present at startup. Packaged resources like criteria_routing.json become unreachable when the release directory is deleted mid-process, causing FileNotFoundError on late resource reads independent of module import caching. Child processes launched via sys.executable fail with FileNotFoundError when the referenced release has been removed between parent startup and child spawn. The wide time window between process start and late imports (e.g., after minutes-long LLM gates) makes this race reachable in production despite being a narrow deletion window.

value.key_entities: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sizing.py::save_checkpoint .rebar/cache/plan-review/<ticket_id> .tmp-{digest}.json envelope.digest tmp.replace(path) tempfile.mkstemp
value.problem_keywords: concurrent writers shared temp file collision checkpoint save atomic write file not found lost checkpoint race condition
value.propositions: save_checkpoint derives a shared temp filename .tmp-{digest}.json keyed by ticket and digest only, not per-writer, causing concurrent writers for the same (ticket, digest) to target the same temp file. When two or more concurrent workers both write and then replace the shared temp file onto the final <digest>.json, the second and later replace calls raise FileNotFoundError because the first replace consumed the temp, and this exception is silently swallowed by the outer except block. The silently swallowed collision causes checkpoints to be lost despite the function's invariant to persist envelopes atomically. The defect mirrors the proven shared-temp collision pattern from ticket 7dea-2f00-db57-4a96 (completion-cache subsystem) and is already remediated on main via commit 6d37024870da1fa4c8be869d1c7113e83bfc214c using tempfile.mkstemp for unique per-writer temps. Concurrent barrier experiments confirm the fix (unique same-directory temp + atomic replace) eliminates collision and residue; pre-fix re-implementation reproduces the collision reliably.

value.propositions: The review-bot webhook and rerun endpoints accept authentication tokens as query parameters, which uvicorn's default access log records in full to stderr/journald in plaintext. value.propositions: Routine MCP backoff events (port-exhausted retire-cap and low-memory abort) emit AUTODEPLOY_ERROR markers that incorrectly inflate deploy_errors counter and false-page the rebar-autodeploy-errors alarm, despite observability.sh contract explicitly stating these should be kept out of deploy_errors. The root cause is record_mcp_backoff_failure() unconditionally calling err deploy_failed on both the two routine backoff paths (~L898-899 mem-abort, ~L907-908 port-exhausted) and genuine failure paths, violating the documented contract introduced in the same commit 2a0a4b19f2ab (ticket 6964). During a burst of merges holding both blue/green MCP ports in graceful drain (2026-08-30 03:33–04:05 UTC), each deploy tick emitted both AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP and AUTODEPLOY_ERROR markers, causing rebar-autodeploy-errors and rebar-autodeploy-mcp-retire-cap alarms to both fire despite no outage and correct safe deferral of cutover. The fix must factor backoff-timer bookkeeping (write MCP_BACKOFF_FILE + prune + throttle) into a shared schedule_mcp_backoff() helper, add record_mcp_routine_backoff() variant for routine paths (schedule + log, no err deploy_failed), and preserve genuine-failure paths (build/tag/run/unhealthy/handshake/flip) emitting deploy_failed. Routine backoff paths must retain the throttle/backoff-file mechanism so deploy ticks don't hammer during a drain; only the erroneous deploy_errors emission is removed. Genuine MCP deploy failures must continue to emit AUTODEPLOY_ERROR and page deploy_errors (no regression in real-failure alarming); regression tests assert routine paths emit their own marker but NOT AUTODEPLOY_ERROR while real failures emit AUTODEPLOY_ERROR.

value.propositions: Attestation staleness messages today name a fixed list (description/AC/file_impact/children) without identifying which component actually changed, preventing operators from finding the edit that caused invalidation. value.key_entities: .github/git-version-floor.txt .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml Git version floor gate step Gerrit Verified lane c433663721 ticket 980d change 1416 tests/conftest.py pytest_configure tests/_git_floor.py .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml
value.problem_keywords: ci gate hard failure tree skew workflow definition vs patchset tree mismatch git version floor false negative in-flight changes
value.propositions: The Git version floor gate step reads .github/git-version-floor.txt from the checked-out patchset tree and hard-errors (exit 1) when the file is absent, but Gerrit's Verified lane sources the workflow definition from the target branch, causing any change branched before the gate merged to fail despite unrelated content. Every open change branched before c433663721 merged carries a false Verified -1 from the gate-definition / tree-content skew; pre-gate changes have no floor file in their tree but get the gate step from the current workflow. The established repository convention (ee2a / Definition-vs-tree skew guard) mandates that new gate steps running repo scripts must skip with a log line when the script is absent from the checked-out tree; the Git-floor gate violates this invariant while two adjacent steps (raw-git-write gate, wall-clock-assert gate) implement it correctly. The fix is to add an if-present guard so an absent floor file skips with an explanatory log line naming the cause (change predates the gate; re-enforces on rebase / post-merge) instead of erroring; under-floor git detection is preserved unchanged. The missing-file failure message must name the real remedy (definition-vs-tree skew, self-heals on rebase) rather than just the filename, so authors do not hunt for a file they never touched. Both tree cases (lacking the floor file and having it) must be verified at runtime by executing the real step, since the workflow-from-main / tree-from-patchset split makes them genuinely different CI scenarios.

value.problem_keywords: git maintenance corruption concurrent writes linked worktree object database detached process invalid object write loss
value.propositions: On git >= 2.47, detached background `git maintenance run --auto` processes escape rebar's write lock and corrupt the shared linked-worktree object database, causing writer commits to fail with 'invalid object' and writes to be lost. Prior fixes (WU-1 gc.autoDetach=true, 4c1c index self-heal) did not address the root cause because git >= 2.47 gates maintenance on `maintenance.auto`, not `gc.auto`, and detached maintenance runs outside the write lock regardless of AutoDetach settings. Disabling background auto-maintenance (`maintenance.auto=false` + `gc.autoDetach=false`) and running serialized gc/maintenance under the write lock prevents concurrent corruption while preserving bounded-growth guarantees. The concurrent write test fails reproducibly on git 2.54 (0 reproductions on 2.47) with 17–232 lost writes per 250 attempts, directly correlated with live detached maintenance repack processes observed during failure. Forward recovery via _recover_from_invalid_object alone cannot heal HEAD-reachable missing objects; a bounded regeneration loop from the intact worktree file is needed alongside disabling background maintenance.

A CI config-validation gate (make config-check in test.yml and gerrit-verify) rejects malformed configuration before it reaches main, preventing runtime apply failures. value.propositions: A push-pending marker persisted from a failed push blocks completion-gated closes even after the backlog has been delivered by another path and refs are provably level. The freshness probe reads the marker state verbatim without reconciling against current git ref divergence, so a stale marker outlives the condition it describes until an ungated write happens to push successfully. Completion gates refuse with stale-store verdict on a healthy store because the marker is never cleared by the refused gate itself, creating a self-sustaining deadlock. The probe has unpushed_count() and _ref_divergence() already computed but does not consult them on the pending branch to validate the marker before asserting a stale verdict. Ticket 16c9-a42d-fd01-48b9 describes this identical defect and was closed with a claimed fix (commit 8c5687af9), but the fix did not land on main and the probe still contains no reconciliation logic.

Attestation staleness messages currently name a fixed, partly-fictional list (description/AC/file_impact/children) instead of identifying which component actually changed, obscuring the root cause. Per-component fingerprints must be stored in the signed manifest as additive material-part lines because children are derived from other tickets' state at read time and cannot be reliably replayed. A pre-330c raw-description attestation can fail grandfather validation on an unchanged ticket due to normalization differences, producing a stale-material verdict with no identifiable component. Completion-verification loop in change 1434 blocks ticket closure despite merged code and all acceptance criteria being met.

value.propositions: A -1 LLM-Review vote blocks a change permanently when the underlying finding (e.g. missing plan-review attestation) is resolved outside the diff. The copy condition (NO_CODE_CHANGE OR MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE OR TRIVIAL_REBASE) causes every re-trigger attempt to copy the stale -1 instead of re-evaluating. Authors must either manufacture unreviewed code changes or request maintainer intervention to clear a stale LLM-Review -1, creating perverse incentives.

value.problem_keywords: gate admission concurrent slots race condition unit test host-global semaphore xdist workers GateCongestedError test isolation
value.propositions: Unit tests exercising gate admission fail with GateCongestedError when four or more pytest-xdist workers run concurrently, because the gate slot directory is host-global and shared across all worktrees and processes on the machine. The gate slot semaphore (/tempdir/locks/) has a fixed capacity of four slots; when real LLM gate operations (review-plan, verify-completion) from other sessions hold slots, concurrent unit tests are refused immediately without queueing. Thirteen known tests fail under parallel execution (-n 4) but pass serially; the failing set varies across runs, confirming a race on shared host resources rather than a deterministic test defect. Re-running failing tests in isolation does not isolate them because REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR defaults to the system tempdir, which is outside the test session's control and shared with production gate work. The gating CI cell uses four xdist workers against four slot capacity, creating risk of spurious Verified -1 verdicts if real gate operations occupy slots during test execution. Providing a per-session private gate slot directory (isolated REBAR_GATE_TMPDIR) resolves the test failures without modifying production gate admission limits.

value.problem_keywords: flaky test concurrent writer git tree-build race git object durability HEAD parse failure shared store lock CI load
value.propositions: Integration test test_concurrent_writer_storm_no_loss fails intermittently under CI load with 8 concurrent subprocess writers racing the shared git store. Writers fail with 'git commit failed while holding lock: error: invalid object' (blob not yet durable) or 'fatal: could not parse HEAD' (unborn/mid-update ref). Race occurs during tree-build or HEAD-parse under the store lock; blobs written by one process are not yet visible to tree-build or ref reads by another. Defect is load-dependent (passes locally on unloaded machine, fails under CI parallelism) and predates recent changes. Root cause is git object-write vs tree-build ordering race in store write path when concurrent processes share one git directory.

value.propositions: Bridge is hard-wired to one tracker project at three points (config, inbound JQL, outbound guard), blocking many-to-many repo-to-project mapping against a shared ticket store. Store-owned project set in `.bridge_state/projects.json` prevents snapshot-diffing collisions when multiple repos fetch disjoint project subsets. Ticket records explicit project (tri-state: absent=legacy, empty=never sync, key=target) and repos; creation targets explicit project over repo default; outbound guards project membership. Pre-feature stores migrate idempotently to legacy default with zero events written; single-project stores remain writable; multi-project stores emit `multi-project-bridge` capability stamp and fail-closed on older binaries. Inbound fetch fans out per configured project, union-merges snapshots, applies per-project truncation; outbound dispatch uses per-ticket project for creates and respects empty-project suppression. `bridge projects` subcommand and library/MCP surfaces provide parity for listing, setting, and removing project→repos mappings.

value.problem_keywords: rich text encoding codec contract adf cloud wiki text data center abstraction seam duplication deployment polymorphism
value.propositions: Cloud REST v3 requires Atlassian Document Format (nested JSON) while Data Center REST v2 uses plain text/wiki markup, creating duplication in map_fields_to_remote across backends. A four-operation RichTextCodec Protocol (fit_outbound, normalize_outbound, to_wire, decode_inbound) must replace hardwired ADF calls so each backend implementation can compose its required steps in the correct order without changing observable behavior. AdfCodec must live in adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py (Cloud-side) and WikiTextCodec in adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py (shared) to satisfy J2's import contract forbidding jira_family from importing Cloud vendor modules. Exactly one real implementation of map_fields_to_remote must exist after this story, relocated to adapters/jira_family/outbound_mapper.py and parameterized by the RichTextCodec dependency, with adapters/jira/backend.py delegating to it. WikiTextCodec truncation limit is 32767 characters with marker ' … [truncated by reconciler]', matching existing constant and adf.py suffix to ensure consistent reader experience across deployments. All four codec operations must be individually testable and proven equivalent to their pre-story implementations for Cloud (via J1 pinned oracles) and new for Data Center.

value.problem_keywords: inbound fetch multi-project jql fan-out source project recording truncation ceiling per-project budget
value.propositions: The inbound fetcher currently builds only one JQL query pair per store mapping despite multiple projects being listed, because jqls_for() accepts a single project key and _validate_project_key rejects empty or malformed keys. The per-query truncation ceiling (_ACLI_CEILING=1200) acts as a shared budget across all projects when a single query is used, allowing one busy project to exhaust capacity on behalf of others. Inbound-created tickets must explicitly record their source project in bridge_project and derive repos from that project's mapping entry, rather than relying only on implicit project encoding in the local id. The solution fans out jqls_for() to issue one JQL pair per project in the store mapping, unions results into a single snapshot, and stamps bridge_project and repos at the inbound CREATE event site in apply_inbound_records.py. The per-project query fan-out keeps the JQL-injection guard from bug 626d applied uniformly to every project key with no new interpolation sites. Single-project store mappings must issue identical query pairs to pre-change behaviour to preserve backward compatibility.

value.component_or_area: store sync and push union guards
value.key_entities: sync._union_merge sync.py:170 push_tickets_branch push.py:216 push.py:242 .store-compat.json epoch field voter.py:719 artifact_emit.py:56 event_append.py:587 write_and_push git merge-base git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json
value.problem_keywords: stale clone store epoch guard union merge non-fast-forward push epoch mismatch fail-closed reclaim safety
value.propositions: A stale clone with stripped history can byte-identically match first 1,029 commits, causing merge-base to succeed and sync.py to take the normal diverged path instead of unrelated-histories, allowing unsafe re-union of ~1 GiB of stripped history. The sync.py guard alone is bypassed because push.py:216 and push.py:242 run independent git merge on non-fast-forward rejection and retry without consulting sync.py, creating a second unsafe union path via the review-bot artifact emit chain. Epoch guard must be placed inside sync._union_merge (shared callee at sync.py:170) and before both non-FF merge calls in push_tickets_branch, but NOT before the merge-base test or at lock.acquire to avoid wedging behind clones or blocking convergence. The epoch field in .store-compat.json must be a JSON string (ISO-8601 UTC instant plus random suffix), compared only for byte equality, never ordered; non-string epochs are corrupt and trigger abort. The complete state matrix (record absent/present × epoch absent/present/unequal/corrupt/unreadable) must distinguish local and remote combinations, with git show failures producing different messages for unreadable refs versus absent files. On epoch mismatch at sync._union_merge, return without merging to leave the clone un-converged; at push.py, return from push_tickets_branch immediately (not break) to exit the retry loop and surface the push as not-completed while preserving both refs byte-for-byte.

value.problem_keywords: usage logging gate run metrics request counting tool call counting loop detection breadth detection tuning data deduplication
value.propositions: Gate runs compute request and tool-call counts internally but discard them before persisting, leaving no durable record for tuning decisions. Loop vs. breadth can be discriminated by the distinct-to-total tool-call ratio, but this signal is computed and dropped one frame from the write. Local gate operators without REBAR_USAGE_LOG set record no usage data at all, forcing re-runs to answer single questions about gate behavior. The usage_log module's existing failure_usage() reducer already computes the complete loop-vs-breadth signal; the defect is that record() accepts the full dict but writes only a fixed allowlist, discarding seven keys. A gate run must durably record what it consumed (requests, tool_calls, limits, duration, ticket_id) on both success and failure paths so operators can tune without instrumentation. The default sink for gate runs must write to the operator's working checkout (.rebar/usage.jsonl) and resolve from repo root, not the throwaway code snapshot, so the record survives and is retrievable.

value.propositions: Landing a change on main does not update the running Gerrit environment; code, replication config, and g2p config require manual deploy and restart, causing drift and operational toil. A systemd timer (every 2 min) must trigger an idempotent, flock-guarded deploy script that fetches origin/main from the mirror and applies only changed components (review-bot, replication, g2p) without touching gerrit container or refs/meta/config. A broken review-bot deploy must be detected by end-to-end health check and immediately rolled back to the previous image; deployed-sha must not advance on failure and circuit-breaker must disable auto-deploy after 2 consecutive failures of the same SHA. Malformed replication or g2p config must be rejected pre-apply via parse validation, prior config retained, and the failure alarmed; config changes use autoReload or materialise, never Gerrit restart. In-flight webhook processing dropped by a bot restart must be recovered by the reconciler backfill (events-log cursor), ensuring reviews are delayed but not lost. A change landing on main must be reflected in the running environment within 5 minutes with no manual action; no-op deploys must be true no-ops and only changed components re-applied.

value.problem_keywords: concurrent writes lost git gc race condition durable write path invalid object background repack exclusive lock
value.propositions: Under heavy concurrent write load, rebar's durable write path loses committed writes when git background gc repacks objects concurrently with writers. Writers holding the exclusive index lock fail git commit with 'invalid object' errors; the write is silently dropped rather than persisted. Background git gc auto-triggers when loose-object count crosses threshold, pruning objects between git add and git commit on concurrent writers. The recovery mechanism (_recover_from_invalid_object) only covers loose objects and fails when missing objects are reachable from HEAD; recovery is one-shot and does not retry. The regression test integration tier flakes at ~75% failure rate on main post-merge CI, blocking Gerrit landings on unrelated changes. The root cause stems from commit f63d72662 re-enabling stock git gc (gc.auto, gc.autoDetach=true) to address loose-object growth; fix requires scoped gc neutralization or hardened recovery loop.

value.problem_keywords: xdist worker death hang loadgroup integration tier job timeout fail fast silent test omission
value.propositions: When an xdist worker crashes under --dist loadgroup in the integration tier, the pytest run does not fail fast but hangs until the job-level 60-minute timeout expires. Worker death under loadgroup causes tests queued on that worker to be silently omitted from the run without notification (e.g., 95 vs 183 collected outcomes). Under --dist worksteal (default-suite tier), xdist replaces dead workers and completes; under loadgroup it does not recover, stalling silently. The hang is amplified by any future worker crash (segfault, OOM, thread watchdog abort), burning the full job cap instead of reporting within seconds. Setting --max-worker-restart=0 on the integration lane makes the first worker death abort the session immediately via triggershutdown instead of re-dispatching.

value.propositions: Landing a change on main does not automatically update the running Gerrit environment; manual deploy via SSM and container restart are currently required, causing operational drift and toil. A circuit-breaker mechanism disables auto-deploy after 2 consecutive failed attempts of the same SHA to prevent thrashing; malformed config is rejected pre-apply and the prior config is retained. Post-deploy health checks verify end-to-end gate functionality (bot receiver endpoint, review path, CI dispatch); rolled-back state is never advanced and in-flight reviews are recovered by reconciler backfill, not lost. Deployed-sha is initialized on first run to current HEAD (adopt state) and written atomically only after success; flock guards against concurrent deploy invocations; observability includes structured logs, deploy_errors metric, and CloudWatch alarms.

value.problem_keywords: many-to-many tracker projects multi-project bridge ticket store project association cross-project sync repo-to-project mapping
value.propositions: The bridge is hard-wired to sync exactly one tracker project per store; teams with multiple projects against one codebase or multiple repos against one store cannot use it. The system must model many-to-many relationships: N repos syncing to N tracker projects via one shared ticket store, with each ticket recording its project and repos. The store owns the project set in `.bridge_state/projects.json` to prevent per-repo project disagreement and remote deletion false positives during multi-project snapshot diffing. Ticket project is tri-state (absent=legacy default, empty=never sync, key=sync to that project); migration uses an idempotent ensure sweep with zero event writes. Multi-project stores carry a `multi-project-bridge` capability stamp in store-compat; older binaries must refuse writes to multi-project stores to prevent duplicate ticket creation.

value.problem_keywords: operator-attested evidence contract measurement provenance wrong environment attestation privilege masking privilege posture simulation vs live-call undeclared measurement context evidence quality gate escape trust boundary
value.propositions: The [operator-attested] evidence contract currently requires attestation-event provenance (change id / vote / timestamp) but not measurement provenance (environment / principal / privilege / instrument), allowing escapes where measurements taken in wrong environments or under broader privilege than production are recorded as settled fact. Two real gate escapes occurred: bedrock measurements taken in account 579718921998 / us-east-2 recorded as fact for work targeting 896586841071 / us-east-1; and live bedrock:Converse calls under bedrock:* identity offered as validation of a scoped bedrock:InvokeModel grant, both satisfying the existing contract but failing in production. The fix extends the [operator-attested] contract with four required measurement-provenance fields (environment, principal, privilege_posture, instrument) declared on an indented continuation line under the checkbox, forcing measurement context into the record as text so repo-grounded machinery can find contradictions. A deterministic check (det_measurement_provenance.py) validates presence and shape of the four provenance fields and their enum membership, while an AGENT-tier criterion (project.measurement-provenance) judges declarations against repo facts (IaC backend anchors, permission scoping, instrument type vs authorization claims). The mechanism ships advisory in the .rebar/ project overlay (not shipped default criteria), preserving existing [operator-attested] tickets without provenance as coaching-only non-blocking, and leaves all four shipped contract-text sites (reviewers/ prompts and coach_moves.py) byte-identical to prevent cross-client behavior change.

value.propositions: A transient GitHub git-fetch hang (2 in 25 runs over 320s) inside repo_snapshot._fetch_origin raises SnapshotFetchError after burning 300s timeout. adapter.code_review_decision's blanket exception handler converts SnapshotFetchError to BLOCK/review-error and votes -1, conflating infrastructure faults with review conclusions. A spurious -1 vote is posted to Gerrit and written to the dedup store, permanently removing the change from backfill re-eligibility because reconcile.py pre-filters on has_llm_review_vote. The vote-less no-vote path already exists and is tested at app.py:161-176 and reconcile.py:222-226, but the inner layer is inconsistent with it. Fix: classify retryable infra exceptions (SnapshotFetchError, TimeoutExpired, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) and return ABSTAIN with no vote, no dedup row, leaving the change vote-less for backfill re-pickup.

value.key_entities: created_at updated_at timestamp signed_at last_reopened_at source_created_at time.time_ns() js_safe_result js_safe_dumps rebar show rebar list rebar sign json.dumps 2**53-1
value.problem_keywords: json serialization nanosecond timestamps big integers float64 rounding js-safe integers rfc 8259 bigint serialization
value.propositions: CLI --output json emits nanosecond timestamps as bare integers exceeding RFC 8259 interoperable range (|n| > 2^53-1), causing silent rounding in float64 consumers (jq, Node, Ruby) and BigInt serialization errors in lossless consumers. MCP surface was fixed by js_safe_result conversion but CLI surface was deliberately excluded from that scope, leaving a pre-existing wire-shape contract gap between three surfaces (MCP, CLI, library). The canonical ticket_state schema already types created_at/updated_at as [integer, string, null] with prose describing the decimal-string wire form for out-of-range integers, but that prose was only true on MCP until Option A adoption. Remediation routes all CLI --output json store-data emitters through a single js_safe_dumps choke point; an out-of-range int is emitted as its exact decimal string, in-range values untouched, conversion is lossless, and an AST guard prevents reintroduction. Two in-repo consumers (reconciler conflict_bug_filing and scripts/alert_dedup) were broken by the string-type change and required coercion with int() to preserve fail-soft semantics; the export_ndjson library boundary was left unchanged and separately tracked. Acceptance criteria require regression coverage pinning both losslessness (int(wire) == stored) and JSON-string type (the direct BigInt-serialization guard), plus an AST enforcement gate to prevent silent drift on future CLI commands.

value.problem_keywords: jira data center support jira server self-hosted jira rest v2 personal access token wiki markup adapter duplication backend seam code sharing
value.propositions: Jira Data Center (self-hosted, REST v2, PAT auth, name-based identity) cannot be reconciled because rebar only supports Cloud (REST v3, ADF, ACLI auth, accountId identity). PR #120 proposed a second adapter that duplicates field maps and sanitizers from adapters/jira/ via private imports, creating an undocumented shared layer without enforced contracts. The field-value maps (status, priority) already exist in three independent copies that have drifted (outbound_fields and config.py include 'deleted: Done'; jira_fields does not), violating single-source principle. The solution consolidates shared logic into adapters/jira_family/ with explicit contracts (RichTextCodec for ADF vs. wiki-markup, UserIdentityModel for accountId vs. name), allowing both Cloud and DC adapters to import from it without cross-dependencies. Location-pinned modules (adf.py, outbound_fields.py, comment_limits.py) must not relocate because they are loaded by path via dynamic loaders; sharing is achieved via dependency inversion (pinned modules import contracts from jira_family/) rather than moving files. The DC backend requires https:// by default, rejects insecure URLs unless allow_insecure=true is set with a warning, never disables certificate verification, and reads the PAT from JIRA_PAT environment variable only (never from config files).

value.problem_keywords: write-time batching commit bloat git object growth event-per-file-per-commit operation packing
value.propositions: Current design commits one mutation per event, creating excessive git objects and unsustainable growth rate at write time. Multiple mutations must be batched into a single git commit per logical operation while preserving per-event identity and append-only CRDT convergence. Batching primitive must preserve replay, dedup, and cross-clone convergence semantics without changing event schema or union-merge behavior. value.key_entities: PYSEC-2026-2132 click 8.2.1 click 8.3.3 click.edit() uv.lock pyproject.toml inspect-ai [eval] extra override-dependencies
value.problem_keywords: pip-audit gating failure dependency vulnerability click PYSEC-2026-2132 command injection blocking verified
value.propositions: The pip-audit gating job fails on every patchset against main due to click 8.2.1 being flagged for PYSEC-2026-2132 (command injection vulnerability in click.edit()). click 8.2.1 is pinned in uv.lock as a transitive dependency constrained by inspect-ai (via [eval] extra), which requires click<8.2.2, making direct lock bump to >=8.3.3 unsatisfiable under standard constraint-dependencies. The vulnerability is unreachable in rebar's codebase: rebar does not import click directly, and click.edit() appears nowhere in source, tests, or scripts. The fix uses uv's override-dependencies to replace inspect-ai's stale click cap, enabling the lock to resolve click 8.4.2, which fixes PYSEC-2026-2132. inspect-ai 0.3.251 (latest) runs cleanly under click 8.4.2 (inspect --help and inspect eval --help both exit 0), proving the upstream cap is stale rather than a real incompatibility.

value.problem_keywords: root disk pressure disk exhaustion docker image accumulation orphaned image tags llm-review fail-close blue-green deployment leak disk reclaim insufficient
value.propositions: Root disk (30 GiB /dev/nvme0n1p1) on rebar-gerrit reached ≥85% used 6 times during 2026-08-29–30 window, triggering rebar-root-disk-pressure alarm; each alarm self-cleared but fail-closed LLM-Review voting. Regression: prior P1 ticket 3a52 (root disk 90% incident) was closed with snapshot-GC watermark fix, but new mcp blue-green deployment family (fd4a, landed 2026-08-25) added a second ~550 MB/deploy tagged-image stream to the same 30 GiB root without corresponding retention strategy, re-filling disk. Root cause: mcp_retire_image and mcp_retire_sweep only retire a compose-mcp:<sha> image when its container is reaped; orphaned tags (container already gone, tag lingering) are never reconciled, causing 16–17 unused tagged images (~9 GB) to accumulate on root. Disk pressure-reclaim (prune_docker_caches) runs continuously (77 prune fires in window) but recovers nothing because it uses `docker image prune -f` (dangling only) and `docker builder prune --keep-storage 5GB` (pinned at 5 GB floor); neither touches tagged images, the actual filler. Root usage floor rose ~30 percentage points (from ~48% post-3a52 to ~78–82% post-fd4a) due to persistent orphaned mcp images; ordinary review/build transients now cross the 85% alarm threshold, whereas previously they did not. Fix implemented: mcp_reconcile_orphans (change 2454 / commit 627faccae8df) added to mcp_retire_sweep to enumerate and retire true orphans post-reap, preserving live image and immediately-previous release for blue-green rollback safety; all tests GREEN; one-time manual reclaim (Part A) freed 4 GB (76%→62%), durable code fix (Part B) prevents recurrence.

value.component_or_area: mutation_gate.py test harness and subprocess isolation
value.key_entities: scripts/mutation_gate.py scripts/mutation_sandbox.py tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py tests/scripts/test_mutation_gate.py execute_shard() _run() _diagnose_non_killed mutmut run pytest sandbox-exec bwrap REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED HOME environment variable CI environment variable
value.problem_keywords: mutation testing sandbox destructive test execution file system protection runtime isolation mutation gate process containment
value.propositions: The mutation gate executes mutated test code unsandboxed, allowing destructive mutations (e.g., removing path guards from deletion scripts) to corrupt the host filesystem up to the point a timeout halts execution. Both the baseline pytest and mutmut run subprocesses spawned by execute_shard() must be wrapped in OS-enforced sandboxes (Seatbelt on macOS, bwrap on Linux) that deny writes outside an explicit allow-list, with the venv deliberately excluded to prevent mutant code injection into site-packages. Sandbox enforcement must be functionally verified—a probe writing outside the allow-list must exit non-zero with the file absent afterward—not merely asserted by inspecting subprocess argv construction. The sandbox mechanism must be verified present AND enforcing on the platform where it runs; Linux bwrap enforcement requires measurement on an actual Linux system where unprivileged user namespaces are available, not inference from macOS results or from green CI runs that skip the enforcement tests. On a workstation with no sandbox mechanism, the mutation gate aborts non-zero naming REBAR_MUTATION_ALLOW_UNSANDBOXED; on a CI runner, it proceeds unsandboxed with a WARNING, treating the CI environment as already disposable. The HOME environment variable is set to a non-existent path for both sandboxed subprocesses so adjacent home-directory writes fail loudly and cannot mask mutations that write to user dotfiles.

value.component_or_area: event store write seam (append_event, finalize_event, reconciler inbound translate)
value.key_entities: src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:329 finalize_event src/rebar/_commands/_seam.py:405 append_event src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:126 _validate_event src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:258-276 src/rebar/secret_screen.py refs/heads/tickets SecretFinding --allow-secret-pattern override
value.problem_keywords: secret leak credential exposure event store write path screening push protection store outage environment dump api keys
value.propositions: Event store accepts event bodies containing live credentials without screening, allowing secrets to propagate to shared git ref and trigger push protection blocks that wedge the entire branch for all concurrent sessions. Write path has four writers reaching the store; append_event is not the only seam — reconciler inbound_translate calls finalize_event halves directly, bypassing append_event — so a screen must live at finalize_event to cover all untrusted input. A deterministic, pure secret screen matches high-confidence patterns (fixed-width windows, line-anchored PEM) tuned by measurement against live store; refused writes emit refusal messages naming family/field/line but never echoing secret values to exception, stdout, stderr, logs, or disk. Force override --allow-secret-pattern=<reason> is CLI-only (not MCP-exposed), recorded on the event with bypassed families for auditability, and available to all write verbs to prevent false positives from permanently blocking legitimate writes describing credentials or security incidents. Benign look-alikes (truncated placeholders, regex literals, prose enumerating banners) verified not to fire on live store sweep (5 matches: all descriptions, zero live credentials), making screen safe to leave enabled by default.

ENOSPC and permanent faults (auth/config/truncation) must remain loud failures and not be reclassified; any disposition split must be narrowly typed to safe-to-retry transport/fetch faults only.

value.key_entities: .store-compat.json format_version required_capabilities KNOWN_CAPABILITIES StoreIncompatibleError check_store_compat() lock.acquire() write_lock() src/rebar/_store/lock.py src/rebar/_commands/fsck_recover.py src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/reconcile.py _apply_mutations() fsck_recover_cli
value.problem_keywords: store compatibility format versioning capability gating fail-closed forward compatibility migration safety rollback safety
value.propositions: rebar lacks a committed store-format-version and required-capability record, allowing old binaries to compute incomplete state from unknown events and emit stale results to Jira or compact operations. A new `.store-compat.json` record with `format_version` and `required_capabilities` must be written atomically at store init and read by a fail-closed gate that blocks unknown versions/capabilities before any mutation. The gate must be inserted at the single convergence point `lock.acquire()` in `src/rebar/_store/lock.py` to cover all lock-held mutations (write_lock context-manager, txn.py, compact.py, fsck.py repair) unconditionally without enumeration. Absent records (pre-v1.0 stores) are treated as legacy format version 0 and pass through without blocking; an idempotent ensure unit writes the record opportunistically at init/fsck-repair/boot so missed sweeps do not block writes. Explicit `check_store_compat()` gates must be added to `fsck_recover_cli` (raw-git mutations without lock) and `reconcile._apply_mutations()` (outbound Jira writes after the persist=True check) to cover mutation paths outside lock.acquire(). Corrupt or unreadable records (JSON parse error, truncation) are fail-closed with a diagnostic message naming the error and path, not treated as absent.

value.problem_keywords: auto-deploy continuous deployment gerrit environment drift manual deploy toil main branch live gate stability
value.propositions: Changes landing on main do not automatically update the running Gerrit environment without manual deploy/restart, causing drift between deployed state and main. A systemd timer-triggered idempotent deploy script must poll origin/main and auto-apply only changed components (review-bot, replication.config, g2p config) without touching the gerrit container or refs/meta/config. Deploy safety requires bounded blast radius (gerrit container untouched, no Gerrit restart), health-check-based rollback on bot failure, and circuit-breaker (disable after 2 consecutive failures of same SHA). In-flight webhook events must not be lost during bot restart; the reconciler backfill re-reviews missed changes, delaying but never dropping contributor votes. Config changes to replication and g2p must be validated (parse-checked) before apply; malformed configs are rejected and prior state retained. Deploy latency must be ≤5 minutes post-main-land; change detection and per-component apply must be idempotent and change-set aware.
